blocks.ar:
بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيْمِ
الحروف المشبهة بالفعل
blocks.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The particles resembling the verb
The particles resembling the verb

blocks.caption: الحروف المشبهة بالفعل
blocks.caption_en: The six particles and their meanings

blocks.en: The above (حروف) particles are called: {{term|الحروف المشبهة بالفعل}} because they have certain characteristics which are exclusive to verbs. Some of those characteristics are:
items: They govern 2 parts of a sentence, one of which they make {{ruling|منصوب}} and the other, they make {{ruling|مرفوع}}.
Their form consists of {{ruling|3 or more letters}}.
They contain meanings which are often found in verbs.
They can have a {{term|ضمير منصوب متصل}} attach to them.
They can also have a {{term|نون الوقاية}} attach to them.
They all end with a {{ruling|فتحة}} resembling الفعل الماضي.

blocks.ar: جملة إسمية / مسند إليه / مسند / خبر
blocks.en: They ONLY enter upon a ({{condition|جملة إسمية}}) sentence (unless deactivated) and make the "مسند إليه" {{ruling|منصوب}} and the "مسند" {{ruling|مرفوع}} if the خبر {{condition|is a noun}}.

Since they enter a (جملة إسمية) sentence, ALL the rules relating to the construction of a (جملة إسمية) sentence such as the {{term|رابط}} rule, the correlation of N/G etc will {{ruling|remain active}}.
The مسند إليه is then termed as "{{term|The Ism of Inna/Anna...}}" ...إسمُ إنَّ/أَنَّ and the مسند as "{{term|The Khabar of Inna/Anna...}}" ...خبرُ إنَّ/أَنَّ.

After they enter the (جملة إسمية) sentence, the construction remains a (جملة إسمية) sentence {{condition|except with Anna أَنَّ}}. The (جملة إسمية) sentence is {{ruling|demoted to a مفرد}} when Anna أَنَّ enters the (جملة إسمية) sentence.
Indeed
Inna, rule 1
items: a) It ONLY enters a ({{condition|جملة إسمية}}) sentence.
b) After it enters the (جملة إسمية) sentence, the construction will remain a ({{ruling|جملة}}) sentence.
c) It gives {{ruling|emphasis}} to the meaning from the perspective of the first person.
d) It will make the "مسند إليه" {{ruling|منصوب}} and it will make the "مسند" {{ruling|مرفوع}} if the مسند {{condition|is a noun}}.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّ اللّٰهَ وَاحِدٌ
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
جملة إسمية: اللّٰهُ وَاحِدٌ
إنَّ + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: Indeed Allah is One. Inna + sentence = sentence
Inna, rule 2
items: a) However, if it's خبر {{condition|is a جملة}}, whether فعلية or إسمية, there will {{ruling|not be any visible effect}} of the الحرف المشبهة بالفعل.
b) The effect will only be {{ruling|assumed}}.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّ اللّٰهَ خَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
جملة إسمية: اللّٰهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ
جملة فعلية: خَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ
إنَّ + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: Indeed Allah created everything. Inna + sentence = sentence
Inna, rule 3
items: a) However, if the مسند {{condition|is a جملة}}, whether فعلية or إسمية, there will {{ruling|not be any visible effect}} of the الحرف المشبهة بالفعل.
b) The effect will only be {{ruling|assumed}}.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّ اللّٰهَ ذَاتُهُ وَاحِدٌ
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
جملة إسمية: اللّٰهُ ذَاتُهُ وَاحِدٌ
جملة إسمية: ذَاتُهُ وَاحِدٌ
إنَّ + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: Indeed Allah, His essence is One. Inna + sentence = sentence
Inna, rule 4
items: a) It is {{ruling|impermissible}} for it's خبر to precede it's إسم unless it's خبر {{condition|is a جار ومجرور or a ظرف}}. In which case, it is {{ruling|permissible but not necessary}}.
b) This rule is not limited to إنَّ, rather it applies to {{ruling|all of the الحروف المشبهة بالفعل}}.
c) Also, an appropriate auxiliary word will be employed.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّ فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدًا
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
جملة إسمية: فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدٌ
جار ومجرور: فِي الدَّارِ
إنَّ + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: Indeed in the house is Zayd. Inna + sentence = sentence
Inna, rule 5
items: a) It is {{ruling|impermissible}} for it's خبر to precede it's إسم unless it's خبر {{condition|is a جار ومجرور or a ظرف}}. In which case, it is {{ruling|permissible but not necessary}}.
b) This rule is not limited to إنَّ, rather it applies to {{ruling|all of the الحروف المشبهة بالفعل}}.
c) Also, an appropriate auxiliary word will be employed.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّ عِنْدَ اللّٰهِ أَعْمَالَنَا
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
جملة إسمية: عِنْدَ اللّٰهِ أَعْمَالُنَا
ظرف: عِنْدَ اللّٰهِ
إنَّ + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: Indeed with Allah are our deeds. Inna + sentence = sentence
Inna, rule 6
items: a) Sometimes a "مَا" is attached to إنَّ.

b) This "مَا" is called "{{term|الكَافَّة}}" (The stopper) because it stops إنَّ from governing. It no longer makes the "مبتدا" منصوب and the "خبر" مرفوع. It absolutely cannot govern anymore. It is {{ruling|totally deactivated}}.
c) This rule applies to all. ({{condition|Except لَيْتَ}})
d) When this happens, إنَّ can enter {{ruling|both (جملة إسمية) & (جملة فعلية)}} sentences.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالسُّوْءِ
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
مَا الكَافَّةُ: مَا
إنَّ + مَا = لَا عَمَل
جملة فعلية: يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالسُّوْءِ
إنَّمَا + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: He only commands you to evil. Inna + maa = no governing. Innamaa + sentence = sentence
Inna, rule 7
items: a) The "مَا الكَافَّة" not only stops the governing of إنَّ, but rather, it stops إنَّ from {{ruling|even having an إسم and a خبر}}.
b) The benefit of the "مَا الكَافَّة" is that, إنَّ, with the "مَا الكَافَّة" provide a meaning of ({{term|حصر}}) exclusivity i.e., together they translate as {{ruling|"only"}}.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّمَا اَللّٰهُ إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
مَا الكَافَّةُ: مَا
إنَّ + مَا = لَا عَمَل
جملة إسمية: اللّٰهُ إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ
إنَّمَا + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: Allah is only One God. Inna + maa = no governing. Innamaa + sentence = sentence
Inna, rule 8
items: a) Sometimes "لَ", a لام signifying {{ruling|emphasis}} is attached to the {{condition|خبر of إنَّ}}.

b) This "لَ" is called "{{term|المُزَحْلَقَة}}" (Moved over) because it was on the مبتدا before إنَّ entered upon it and was originally known as "{{term|لام الإبتِداء}}". However, it was moved over to the خبر of إنَّ {{condition|to avoid two consecutive words signifying emphasis}}.
c) The "لام المُزَحْلَقَة" is {{ruling|exclusive to إنَّ}}.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّ زَيدًا لَجَالِسٌ
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
اللام المزحلقة: لَ
جملة إسمية: لَزَيْدٌ جَالِسٌ
إنَّ + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: Indeed Zayd is surely sitting. Inna + sentence = sentence
Inna, rule 9
items: a) The "لام المُزَحْلَقَة" can attach to a verb if a verb is the خبر of إنَّ provided the verb is {{condition|not preceded by a negation}} i.e., the verb must be {{ruling|مثبت}} and not منفي.
b) There are more conditions for this لام to attach to verbs correctly, one of which has been mentioned above. We will discuss them in the future Insha'Allah.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّ زَيدًا لَيَجْلِسُ
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
اللام المزحلقة: لَ
جملة إسمية: لَزَيْدٌ يَجْلِسُ
إنَّ + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: Indeed Zayd surely sits. Inna + sentence = sentence
Inna, rule 10
items: a) The "لام المُزَحْلَقَة" can attach to the {{ruling|إسم of إنَّ}} if the {{condition|خبر of إنَّ precedes the إسم of إنَّ}} for the same reason of avoiding two consecutive words signifying emphasis.

blocks.ar:
إِنَّ فِي الدَّارِ لَزَيدًا
الحرف المشبهة بالفعل: إنَّ
اللام المزحلقة: لَ
جملة إسمية: لَزَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ
إنَّ + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: Indeed in the house is surely Zayd. Inna + sentence = sentence
Rules relating to "لام المُزَحْلَقَة" will be revisited in the future InshaAllah.
That... | Indeed

items: a) It ONLY enters a ({{condition|جملة إسمية}}) sentence.
b) The (جملة إسمية) sentence it enters will become a ({{ruling|مفرد}}) compound/phrase.
c) Together أَنَّ with it's إسم and خبر will ALWAYS fall into places of {{ruling|مفرد}}.
d) It also gives emphasis to the meaning from the perspective of the first person.
e) It will make the "مسند إليه" {{ruling|منصوب}} and it will make the "مسند" {{ruling|مرفوع}} if the مسند is a noun.

blocks.en: I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

items: a) If it's خبر is a {{condition|جملة}}, whether فعلية or إسمية, there will not be any visible effect of the الحرف المشبهة بالفعل. The effect will only be {{ruling|assumed}}.

blocks.ar: مِنْ اِعْتِقَادِيْ أَنَّ اللهَ خَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ
blocks.en: Of my belief is that Allah created everything.

items: a) If it's خبر is a {{condition|جملة}}, whether فعلية or إسمية, there will not be any visible effect of the الحرف المشبهة بالفعل. The effect will only be {{ruling|assumed}}.

blocks.en: I believe that Allah, His essence is one.

items: a) It is {{ruling|impermissible}} for it's خبر to precede it's إسم unless it's خبر is a {{condition|جار ومجرور}} or a {{condition|ظرف}}. In which case, it is permissible but not necessary.
b) This applies to all the الحروف المشبهة بالفعل.
c) Also, an appropriate auxiliary word will be employed.

blocks.en: It pleased me that in the house is Zayd.

items: a) It is {{ruling|impermissible}} for it's خبر to precede it's إسم unless it's خبر is a {{condition|جار ومجرور}} or a {{condition|ظرف}}. In which case, it is permissible but not necessary.
b) This applies to all the الحروف المشبهة بالفعل.
c) Also, an appropriate auxiliary word will be employed.

blocks.en: Indeed, with Allah are our deeds.

items: a) The "{{term|مَا الكَافَّة}}" can also attach to أَنَّ but will not affect the ability of أَنَّ converting the sentence to {{ruling|مفرد}}.
b) It will stop أَنَّ from {{ruling|governing}} the مبتدا and خبر. It will no longer make the "مبتدا" منصوب and the "خبر" مرفوع.
c) When this happens, أَنَّ can enter both, ({{ruling|جملة إسمية}}) & ({{ruling|جملة فعلية}}), sentences.

blocks.ar: أَ فَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَا كُمْ عَبَثًا
blocks.en: Did you then think that We created you in play?

items: a) The "مَا الكَافَّة" not only stops the governing of أَنَّ, but also stops أَنَّ from even having an {{ruling|إسم}} and a {{ruling|خبر}}.
b) The benefit of ({{term|حصر}}) exclusivity the "مَا الكَافَّة" provided when connected to إِنَّ is also found with أَنَّ prominently.
c) The "مَا الكَافَّة" will not affect the ability of أَنَّ converting the sentence to {{ruling|مفرد}}.

blocks.ar: إِنَّمَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَا إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ
blocks.en: It is only revealed to me that your god is one God.

items: a) The ability of أَنَّ in converting the sentence after it into مفرد adds أَنَّ to another group of words known as {{term|الموصولات الحرفية}} which share this same characteristic of converting sentences into مفرد.
b) This process is called: {{term|بِتَأْوِيل المصدر/المفرد}} (BTM) often manifesting as {{ruling|المركب الإضافي}}.
We will discuss this soon Insha'Allah!

blocks.en: It pleased me that Zayd is a Muslim.
Like | As if...

items: a) It ONLY enters a ({{condition|جملة إسمية}}) sentence.
b) After it enters the (جملة إسمية) sentence, the construction will remain a ({{ruling|جملة}}).
c) It gives the meaning of it's إسم {{term|resembling}} it's خبر with emphasis.
d) It will make the "مسند إليه" {{ruling|منصوب}} and the "مسند" {{ruling|مرفوع}} if the مسند is a noun.

blocks.en: As if Zayd is a lion.

items: a) It will not visibly affect it's خبر if it is a {{condition|sentence}} just as إِنَّ and أَنَّ didn't visibly affect their خبر when it was a sentence.
b) The affect will be {{ruling|assumed}}.

blocks.en: As if Zayd is reading the Qur'an.

items: a) Rules relating to it's خبر preceding it's إسم are identical to those mentioned in إِنَّ and أَنَّ.
b) It is only when it's خبر is a {{condition|جار ومجرور}} or a {{condition|ظرف}} that it becomes {{ruling|permissible}} for it's خبر to precede it's إسم otherwise not.
c) This applies to all of the الحروف المشبهة بالفعل.
d) Also, an appropriate auxiliary word will be employed.

blocks.en: As if Zayd is with you.

items: e) The rules relating to "{{term|مَا الكَافَّة}}" are also identical to إِنَّ and أَنَّ in stopping the governing of كَأَنَّ.
a) However, there is {{ruling|no added benefit}} of the meaning of (حصر) exclusivity here.
b) When this happens, كَأَنَّ can enter both (جملة إسمية) & (جملة فعلية) sentences. Just like إِنَّ and أَنَّ, it will no longer be restricted to a جملة إسمية construction.

blocks.en: As if they are being driven to death.
{{term|However}}|{{term|But}}
The particles resembling the verb: lakinna
Lakinna, 1
items: a) It ONLY enters a ({{condition|جملة إسمية}}) sentence.
b) After it enters the (جملة إسمية) sentence, the construction will remain a ({{ruling|جملة}}).
c) It also adds a meaning of {{ruling|emphasis}} to the sentence and comes between two contrasting sentences to correct a potential assumption. ({{term|استدراك}})
d) It will make the “مسند إليه” {{ruling|منصوب}} the “مسند” {{ruling|مرفوع}} if the مسند is a noun.

blocks.en: Bakr is absent, but Zayd is present.
lakinna + sentence = {{ruling|sentence}}
Lakinna, 2
items: a) It will {{ruling|not visibly affect}} it’s خبر {{condition|if it is a sentence}} just as إِنَّ, أَنَّ and كَأَنَّ didn’t visibly affect their خبر when it was a sentence.
b) The effect will be {{ruling|assumed}}.

blocks.ar: جاءَ زَيْدٌ لكِنَّهُ لَمْ يَدْخُلْ البَيْتَ
blocks.en: Zayd came, but he did not enter the house.
lakinna + sentence = {{ruling|sentence}}
The particles resembling the verb: lakinna
Lakinna, 3
items: c) Rules relating to it’s خبر preceding it’s إسم are identical to those mentioned in إِنَّ, أَنَّ and كَأَنَّ.
d) When it’s خبر is a {{condition|جار ومجرور}} or a {{condition|ظرف}}, only then does it become {{ruling|permissible}} for it’s خبر to precede it’s إسم otherwise not.
e) This applies to all of the {{term|الحروف المشبهة بالفعل}}.
f) Also, an appropriate auxiliary word will be employed.

blocks.en: I have a pen, but you have paper.
lakinna + sentence = {{ruling|sentence}}
Lakinna, 4
items: a) The rules relating to “{{term|مَا الكَافَّة}}” are also identical to إِنَّ, أَنَّ and كَأَنَّ in {{ruling|stopping the governing}} of لكِنَّ.
b) However, there is {{ruling|no added benefit}} of the meaning of ({{term|حصر}}) exclusivity here.
c) When this happens, لكِنَّ can enter {{ruling|both}}, (جملة إسمية) & (جملة فعلية), sentences. Just like إِنَّ, أَنَّ and كَأَنَّ, it will no longer be restricted to a جملة إسمية construction.

blocks.ar: أَكَلَ زَيْدٌ لكِنَّمَا لَمْ يَأْكُلْ إِبْنُهُ
blocks.en: Zayd ate, but his son did not eat.

blocks.ar: لكِنَّ + مَا = {{ruling|لَا عَمَل}}، لكِنَّمَا + جملة = جملة
blocks.en: lakinna + maa = {{ruling|no governing}}; lakinnamaa + sentence = sentence
{{term|I wish}}
The particles resembling the verb: layta
Layta, 1
items: a) It ONLY enters a ({{condition|جملة إسمية}}) sentence.
b) After it enters the (جملة إسمية) sentence, the construction will remain a ({{ruling|جملة}}).
c) It gives the meaning of {{ruling|wishing}} from the perspective of the {{ruling|first person}}.
d) It is used for {{ruling|impossible scenarios}} more often than possible ones.
e) It will make the “مسند إليه” {{ruling|منصوب}} and the “مسند” {{ruling|مرفوع}} if the مسند is a noun.

blocks.en: I wish Zayd were alive.
layta + sentence = sentence ({{ruling|inshaa'iyyah}})
Layta, 2
items: a) It will {{ruling|not visibly affect}} it’s خبر {{condition|if it is a sentence}} just as إِنَّ, أَنَّ, كَأَنَّ and لكِنَّ didn’t visibly affect their خبر when it was a sentence.
b) The effect will be {{ruling|assumed}}.

blocks.en: I wish I had done it.
layta + sentence = sentence ({{ruling|inshaa'iyyah}})
The particles resembling the verb: layta
Layta, 3
items: a) Rules relating to it’s خبر preceding it’s إسم are identical to those mentioned in إِنَّ, أَنَّ, كَأَنَّ and لكِنَّ.
b) When it’s خبر is a جار ومجرور or a {{condition|ظرف}}, only then does it become {{ruling|permissible}} for it’s خبر to precede it’s إسم otherwise not.
c) This applies to all of the {{term|الحروف المشبهة بالفعل}}.
d) Also, an appropriate auxiliary word will be employed.

blocks.en: I wish we had a sincere ruler.
layta + sentence = sentence ({{ruling|inshaa'iyyah}})
Layta, 4
items: a) Rules relating to it’s خبر preceding it’s إسم are identical to those mentioned in إِنَّ, أَنَّ, كَأَنَّ and لكِنَّ.
b) When it’s خبر is a {{condition|جار ومجرور}} or a ظرف, only then does it become {{ruling|permissible}} for it’s خبر to precede it’s إسم otherwise not.
c) This applies to all of the {{term|الحروف المشبهة بالفعل}}.
d) Also, an appropriate auxiliary word will be employed.

blocks.en: I wish Zayd were in the world.
layta + sentence = sentence ({{ruling|inshaa'iyyah}})
The particles resembling the verb: layta
Layta, 5
items: e) The rules relating to “{{term|مَا الكَافَّة}}” are {{ruling|different}} to إِنَّ, أَنَّ, كَأَنَّ and لكِنَّ.
f) The effect of the “مَا الكَافَّة” upon لَيتَ is {{ruling|optional}}.

a) So, what that means is that لَيتَ can seize to govern it’s إسم and خبر and allow them to revert back to {{label|مبتدء}} and {{label|خبر}} OR it can continue to govern it’s إسم and خبر and make them {{ruling|منصوب}} and {{ruling|مرفوع}} respectively.

blocks.en: I wish youth were returning.

blocks.ar: لَيْتَ + مَا = {{ruling|لَا عَمَل}}، لَيْتَمَا + جملة = جملة (إنشائية)
blocks.en: layta + maa = {{ruling|no governing}}; laytamaa + sentence = sentence (inshaa'iyyah)
Layta, 6
items: b) There is {{ruling|no added benefit}} of the meaning of ({{term|حصر}}) exclusivity here.
c) When the “مَا الكَافَّة” is attached to لَيتَ, then unlike its homogeneous counterparts, لَيتَ will {{ruling|remain restricted}} to a {{condition|جملة إسمية}}.
d) Despite the presence of the “مَا الكَافَّة”, It will {{ruling|not enter}} a جملة فعلية.

blocks.en: I wish youth were returning.
layta + maa = {{ruling|governing}}; laytamaa + sentence = sentence (inshaa'iyyah)
{{term|Perhaps/Hopefully}}
The particles resembling the verb: la'alla

items: a) It ONLY enters a ({{condition|جملة إسمية}}) sentence.
b) After it enters the (جملة إسمية) sentence, the construction will remain a ({{ruling|جملة}}).
f) It gives the meaning of {{term|hope}}, {{term|concern}} and {{term|reason}} from the perspective of the first person.
c) It will make the “مسند إليه” {{ruling|منصوب}} and the “مسند” {{ruling|مرفوع}} {{condition|if the مسند is a noun}}.

blocks.en: Perhaps the lesson is easy.

items: a) It will {{ruling|not visibly affect}} it’s خبر {{condition|if it is a sentence}} just as إِنَّ, أَنَّ, كَأَنَّ, لكِنَّ and لَيتَ didn’t visibly affect their خبر when it was a sentence.
b) The effect will be {{ruling|assumed}}.

blocks.en: Perhaps I will fail in the exam.
The particles resembling the verb: la'alla

items: a) Rules relating to it’s خبر preceding it’s إسم are identical to those mentioned in إِنَّ, أَنَّ, كَأَنَّ, لكِنَّ and لَيتَ.
c) When it’s خبر is a {{condition|جار ومجرور}} or a {{condition|ظرف}}, only then does it become {{ruling|permissible}} for it’s خبر to precede it’s إسم otherwise not.
d) This applies to all of the الحروف المشبهة بالفعل.
e) Also, an appropriate auxiliary word will be employed.

blocks.en: Perhaps the students are in the school.

items: a) The rules relating to “{{term|مَا الكَافَّة}}” in stopping the governing of لَعَلَّ are also identical to إِنَّ, أَنَّ, كَأَنَّ and لكِنَّ.
b) There is {{ruling|no added benefit}} of the meaning of (حصر) exclusivity.

c) When this happens, لَعَلَّ can enter {{ruling|both (جملة إسمية) & (جملة فعلية)}} sentences. Just like إِنَّ, أَنَّ, كَأَنَّ and لكِنَّ, it will no longer be restricted to a جملة إسمية construction.

Summary

items: All of الحروف المشبهة بالفعل {{ruling|only enter upon a جملة إسمية}}.
The جملة remains a جملة except with {{condition|أَنَّ}} where the جملة becomes {{ruling|مفرد}}.
They make the “مسند إليه” {{ruling|منصوب}} and the “مسند” {{ruling|مرفوع}}.
The مبتدا is called their {{term|إسم}} and the خبر is called their {{term|خبر}}.
The rules of مبتدا & خبر such as correlating in N/G and خبر being مفرد or جملة etc are all {{ruling|retained}}
Their خبر can’t precede their إسم {{condition|unless the خبر is a جار ومجرور or ظرف}}.
The “{{term|مَا الكَافَّة}}” can attach to them and prevent them from governing, from making the “مبتدا” مرفوع and the “خبر” منصوب.
When the “مَا الكَافَّة” is attached, then they are not restricted to a جملة إسمية. They can then enter upon a {{ruling|جملة فعلية}} as well.
{{term|لَيْتَ}} is exempt as it remains restricted to the جملة إسمية and therefore the prevention imposed by the “مَا الكَافَّة” is {{ruling|optional}}.

blocks.en: Further Rules in relation to الحروف المشبهة بالفعل
1. ضمير منصوب متصل
As we already know, a ضمير منصوب متصل generally connects to verbs as a {{label|مفعول به}}, e.g., ضَرَبْتُهُ

As mentioned before, a ضمير منصوب متصل can also connect to الحروف المشبهة بالفعل, e.g., إِنَّهُ – كَأَنَّهَا – لَعَلَّهُمَا. Since this is a characteristic of verbs, this was also one of the reasons for the name given to these particles.

From amongst the ضمير منصوب متصل, when the ي متكلم connects to a verb, a {{term|نون الوقاية}} comes in-between the verb and the ي in order to protect the verb from {{ruling|كسرة}}. (This because the كسرة is exclusive to nouns as we already know) e.g., ضَرَبَنِيْ

Due to their resemblance to verbs, the نون الوقاية can also come in-between الحروف المشبهة بالفعل and the ي متكلم when the ي متكلم is connected to these particles. e.g., إِنَّنِي – كَأَنَّنِي – لَيْتَنِي. Unlike verbs, where the presence of the نون الوقاية is {{ruling|necessary}}, its presence is {{ruling|always optional}} with the الحروف المشبهة بالفعل.

blocks.en: 2. اللام المزحلقة

As mentioned before, a لام can be added to the {{condition|خبر of إِنَّ}} to provide {{ruling|further emphasis}}. This لام has been termed {{term|المزحلقة}} which means: The one which has been made to move over. Etymologically, the word is a {{term|رباعي}}, on the pattern of فَعْلَلَ يُفَعْلِلُ – زَحْلَقَ يُزَحْلِقُ meaning to move over, to slide, to push, to slip. The word مُزَحْلَقَةٌ is the single feminine form of the {{term|إسم المفعول}} (PPA).
